text:
marta: FYI we rolled the new continuous-batching heuristic into serving-pool-a ~03:09 UTC and within ~2m saw p95 latency jump ~2x and sustained throughput drop ~20%. Appears tied to queue backpressure and KV cache activity.

josh: ugh. which flag exactly? can you paste the deploy id?

marta: deploy id c-batcher-v2-2026-03-18-0309. deploy-bot shows: 

deploy-bot: rolled c-batcher-v2 to serving-pool-a at 2026-03-18T03:09:42Z

kai: quick ask — did we also flip any kernel-affinity changes? last week's kernel selector tweak was on the same branch.

marta: no kernel selector on that commit, just batch heuristics (queue aging, token-budget target lowered for short requests). logs attached below.

ravi: dropping some profiler numbers I grabbed from the slow window:
- small-batch kernel usage ↑ 38%
- avg batch size down from 8.2 -> 5.1
- KV cache miss rate ↑ 2.6x on shard-12
- GPU occupancy flat, GPU SM util steady, but host-side CPU queue thread stalled more often

kai: KV miss jump + smaller batches smells like we changed batching windowing such that requests are being flushed before KV prefetch completes. Could be prefetch timing or backpressure on the async fetch path.

marta: here's a short log excerpt around the spike (trimmed):

```
03:10:03.112 [batcher] pool=a shard=12 batch_size=3 flush_reason=budget_short token_budget=12
03:10:03.113 [kv-fetch] shard=12 req=0x7ff evict=0 miss=true backend_latency_ms=12.8
03:10:03.114 [kernel] selected=small_batch_kernel reason=batch_shape
03:10:03.118 [batcher] pool=a batch_size=2 flush_reason=timeout queued=6
03:10:03.120 [latency] request_id=0x7ff p95=198ms baseline=95ms
03:10:03.220 [kv-fetch] shard=12 req=0x800 evict=1 miss=true backend_latency_ms=24.3
```

marta: note repeated small batches and KV backend latencies piling up.

josh: can we repro locally by forcing artificial KV backend latency and the new budget targets?

kai: yes, we can run a microbench with a KV stub. I suspect the new token_budget threshold causes early flush, starving the async prefetch pipeline.

ravi: quick mitigation suggestion: increase token_budget target for short requests by +50% or add a short prefetch gating delay (10ms) so KV responses land before flush.

marta: did a quick canary: disabled c-batcher-v2 on 10% of traffic at 03:17 UTC and p95 on that canary returned to baseline within 30s. Confirmed rollback on the canary removed the latency spike.

alert-bot: serving-pool-a p95 latency exceeded 150ms threshold (03:11-03:18 UTC)

josh: ok that's strong signal. Plan: 1) roll back pool-a to previous batcher config (v1) 2) run isolated microbench with KV stall to reproduce 3) test two fixes: raise token budget vs prefetch gating. Who wants to own the repro?

kai: I'll own the repro and bench harness. I'll spin a KV stub that can inject 5-30ms tail latencies and run the same arrival distribution.

ravi: I'll prototype increasing the budget and a tiny gating delay on the prefetch path in parallel. If gating removes miss amplification that's the better long-term fix.

marta: I'll coordinate rollback and keep SRE informed. Rolling back pool-a now. Please post results here, especially profiler snapshots and batch-size distribution.

josh: thanks team. follow-up RFC to cover kernel affinity + batching interplay so we don't have hidden cross-effects. :thumbsup:

marta: TL;DR: new batching heuristic caused premature flushes -> smaller batches -> higher KV miss amplification -> latency spike. Canary rollback confirms. Next: repro + fix proposals.

kai: ETA for repro 2 hours, will post artifacts.

ravi: I'll have a patch/bench by EOD.

marta: awesome — assigning a follow-up ticket and linking perf graphs. I'll ping infra-alloc if we need extra GPU for bench.

josh: leave a note to check continuous-batching metrics (batch_size_histogram, flush_reasons, kv_miss_rate) in dashboards; add an alert for sudden batch size drops.

marta: added that alert. closing for now once pool rollback stabilizes.
